preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Advance release convergence with readable cemetery presentation, measurable and stable dense native performance, and a complete traversable run with truthful spatial bounds, retry lifecycle, and authored upgrade-choice presentation.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate remains underlit against the bound cemetery composition target, lacks native 1920x1080 dense-run qualification and retry-growth evidence, and still needs complete-route spatial/lifecycle proof. The world repair must use authored-instance, collision, outer-datum, and visibility-contract work rather than another camera transform pass.

stop_conditions: Preserve the native authored cemetery package and validated meshes; do not replace, split, hide, or reposition authored child geometry.
Do not schedule deferred camera-occlusion work as a standalone task or expand beyond the three bounded families.
Do not claim issue closure from instrumentation or static checks alone; stop after Tester/GameLoop Runtime obtains matched black-box and white-box retests.

strategy.rationale: Partition the exact required gaps into scene exposure, dense performance, and complete-run release families. Repair exposure through environment/light/material binding, qualify performance through bounded measurement plus measured lifecycle/render fixes, and restore complete-route spatial/lifecycle behavior around the preserved authored world. Carry both hard player capabilities into the relevant release task.

code: Run candidate import/parse checks and preserve validate:native_godot_project plus validate:host_godot_boot.

Run focused checks for lighting resource validity, dense-profile counter bounds, pool/reset invariants, single-shot terminal transitions, collision masks, and upgrade-draft current/result normalization.
Verify no raw imported source asset is modified.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime/Tester recaptures spawn, critical route, near-contact, after-departure, dense stress, boss transition, victory/result, death/result, and Retry states with runtime_state, frame-time/entity receipts, and error-log probes.

Retest finding.arena_exposure_readability and finding.dense_profile_native_gap with matched camera/framing and native 1920x1080 stress conditions; require direct behavior plus candidate-side receipts before closure.
Replay ordinary movement around the central building, landmarks, and full perimeter to verify collision, boundary containment, stable visibility, and clean reset.
Run distinct successful ordinary routes for focused lantern, close-range gravespade, and orbiting wisps; use failure only for failure/result/retry qualification.
visual: Compare sparse shipped-camera views against the bound reference properties: high-angle framing, readable escape lanes, coherent cemetery density, warm-versus-cool lighting hierarchy, distinct silhouettes, and compact authored HUD.

Inspect level-up cards at native viewport, windowed/fullscreen, configured UI scales, and keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states; verify silhouettes, icons, truthful current-to-new deltas, and no text-stacked placeholders.
Inspect result and Retry pages for full-viewport composition, focus continuity, no stale overlays, and no clipped or debug-like labels.

done_when: Fresh gameplay at spawn, critical route, dense combat, and cardinal landmark views has readable moonlit blue-violet shadows, warm lantern accents, streets, escape lanes, player/enemy silhouettes, pickups, and hazards.

The lighting hierarchy is visibly closer to the bound Mournlight composition target without flattening hostile telegraphs or introducing placeholder/proxy geometry, and import/runtime logs remain clean.
Tester can recapture the same shipped gameplay camera and framing for direct before/after retest.
tasks.instructions: Repair runtime cemetery exposure at the scene/environment binding layer. Inspect WorldEnvironment, moon key/fill, landmark pools, fog, emission, and contrast relationships; correct the underlit hierarchy with deterministic, budgeted settings. Preserve native streets, props, landmarks, and materials, and keep player lantern, enemy accents, danger telegraphs, and escape lanes readable at representative density. Use a scene-level exposure correction rather than transform tuning.
tasks.title: Restore moonlit cemetery exposure and landmark readability

done_when: A deterministic native 1920x1080 stress replay reaches 25-40 ordinary enemies with all three weapon families, pickups, UI, VFX, lights, audio, and boss behavior active, and emits frame-time distribution plus active/pooled entity counters.

The stress path shows no recurring runtime errors, invalid freed-instance access, unbounded node/signal/audio growth, or gameplay-semantic changes to spawn, damage, targeting, wave, upgrade, or boss transitions.
Three complete retries return frame-time, active counts, timers, pause state, seed/session generation, HUD state, audio voices, and pooled actors to a stable baseline.
tasks.instructions: Make dense-run performance closure-ready. Instrument authoritative wave/director, actor/pool, projectile/pickup/effect, physics-query, and HUD update paths with lightweight bounded counters and frame-time sampling, then apply only measured fixes such as pooling reset completion, staggered queries, capped effects/lights/voices, or safe scheduling. Expose a deterministic stress checkpoint while preserving hit causality, telegraphs, target legality, and wave pacing.
tasks.title: Qualify and stabilize native dense-run performance

done_when: The ordinary route can expand to a larger traversable scale from spawn through all waves, Bellkeeper boss, result, and Retry without void exposure or camera-occlusion drift.

The external world or external depth remains visible beyond the playable boundary, while the central building and every gameplay-relevant landmark retain stable visibility before approach, at near contact, and after departure.

Collision agrees with visible geometry and the boundary/perimeter: ordinary movement and movement replay cannot pass through landmarks, leave the playable area, hide actors inside geometry, or cause landmark disappearance.

Run lifecycle reaches death/result and victory/result exactly once, then Retry/reset clears enemies, pools, timers, pause ownership, upgrades, seed/session state, audio, and HUD state before a fresh run.

Level-up choices use an authored visual hierarchy with weapon or upgrade silhouettes and compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, no NEW or LOCKED placeholder in the CURRENT column, and complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states.
tasks.instructions: Restore the complete release route using the preserved authored cemetery package as the sole authoritative visual world. Expand to a larger traversable scale through package framing, native-street spawn/objective anchors, navigation, collision, and one outer datum; retain external world/external depth beyond the boundary without proxy floors or duplicate map families. Verify the central building/landmark collision and visibility contract during ordinary movement and movement replay so there is no disappearance or whole-landmark occlusion. Complete wave, boss, result, death/result, and clean Retry/reset behavior. Audit upgrade-draft presentation in the same release-shell pass, making only narrow fixes needed for the authored visual hierarchy and input-focus contract.
tasks.title: Complete run with spatial integrity, landmark visibility, and retry shell
